clue.text: Chief US agents sent back, being behind the times

parts.note: arch- means chief or principal, as in archbishop

indicators.note: sent back tells us the agents' letters are turned round and read the other way

parts.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A complaint that America's top spies, recalled home, are hopelessly out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind the times' looks like a description of the agents, but it is the definition; 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic belongs to an earlier age, so it is old-fashioned and out of step with modern life.

clue.text: Agree to take notes

parts.note: read the word as a string of six musical notes, ..., and it also means to consent

explanation.surface: A student consents to write down what is said in a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole answer is spelt out in note names from the musical scale, so 'take notes' describes its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a request is to consent to it.

clue.text: Tea ready? I will get the bread

parts.note: cha is an informal word for tea
pat means ready or prepared, as in having an answer off pat

explanation.surface: Someone asks if tea is ready and promises to bring the bread.
explanation.walkthrough: PAT for 'ready' comes from 'off pat', known and ready to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: A heavy depositor in Swiss banks?

definitions.text: A heavy depositor in Swiss banks?

parts.words: A heavy depositor in Swiss banks?
parts.note: the banks are mountain slopes in Switzerland, and the depositor dumps a great weight of snow on them, not money

explanation.walkthrough: Swiss banks suggest secret accounts and wealthy clients; here banks are slopes of the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountainside deposits a huge load at the bottom.

clue.text: Steel band used to make this track

definitions.text: Steel band used to make this track

parts.words: Steel band used to make this track
parts.note: not a Caribbean band recording a song, but a continuous loop of steel plates that a tracked vehicle runs on

explanation.surface: A steel band recording a song in the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steel band' and 'track' suggest music; the track is the endless belt of a bulldozer or tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterpillar track is the jointed steel belt fitted round the wheels of tanks and tractors.

clue.text: Enclosed area near stern that is needed in the main

definitions.text: Enclosed area near stern that is needed in the main

parts.words: Enclosed area near stern that is needed in the main
parts.note: the main is the open sea, and on a yacht the sunken well near the stern is where the crew steer from

explanation.surface: A description of a vital space at the back of something, essential to the main operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the sea, which explains why a boat's steering area is needed there.
explanation.definitionFit: On a small sailing boat the steering well near the stern is called by this name, as is a pilot's compartment.

clue.text: Golly! This king is splendid!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation one might make on seeing something impressive, an admiring 'wow'

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are exclamations; the second is what someone says when impressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise or admiration, a slang form of 'God'.

clue.text: Impudence from upper layer of society

definitions.meaning: cheek or nerve, the nerve to say something rude
the upper class, as in the phrase 'upper ...'

explanation.surface: A complaint about cheek coming from the posh set.
explanation.definitionFit: Crust is slang for cheek or nerve, and is also the hard outer layer, hence the upper crust of society.

clue.text: Security device to keep squatters out?

definitions.text: Security device to keep squatters out?

parts.words: Security device to keep squatters out?
parts.note: a pad is slang for a home, so a lock on the pad keeps squatters away

explanation.surface: A homeowner wondering what will stop squatters moving in.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer's first syllable as 'pad', slang for a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachable lock with a hinged shackle is a common security device for doors and gates.

clue.text: A ruse concocted in attempt to get funds

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt

indicators.note: concocted means made up or cooked up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A con trick is cooked up in a bid to obtain money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concocted' turns A RUSE into REASU, which goes 'in' TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasury is a store of money or the revenue of a state.

clue.text: Letter or card

definitions.meaning: a single printed symbol of the alphabet
an eccentric or amusing person, as in 'he's a card'

explanation.definitionFit: A character is a written symbol, and also an odd, colourful person.

clue.text: Excessive force used to keep peace? Exactly!

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces
due means exactly, as in due north

explanation.surface: A complaint that a peacekeeping force went too far, followed by a firm agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: DUE as 'exactly' comes from compass directions: due east is precisely east.
explanation.definitionFit: Undue means more than is warranted, so unreasonably great.

clue.text: Play part of Phaedra, maybe

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taking a role in Phaedra, the classical tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage.

clue.text: Food supplies divided by the Spanish family

indicators.note: divided by says the word for food supplies is split with the other piece set inside it

parts.note: rations are fixed allowances of food
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A Spanish family shares out its food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'family' could be read with 'the Spanish' as a Spanish family; 'the Spanish' only supplies the Spanish article.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations are relatives, the members of one's family.

clue.text: Seaman protected by Republican advocate of freedom

indicators.note: protected by means the sailor sits inside the other word, sheltered by it

parts.note: a Liberian is a citizen of the Republic of Liberia
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor sheltered by a Republican who champions liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests a US party; here it is a citizen of the Republic of Liberia.
explanation.definitionFit: A libertarian believes in maximum individual liberty.

clue.text: Safety device destroyer used on exercises

indicators.note: used on means the destroyer word is placed after the exercise word in this across clue

parts.note: circuit training is a sequence of exercises
a breaker is one who breaks or destroys

explanation.surface: A warship deployed during military exercises, described as a safeguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyer' looks like a warship but is just one who breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: This switch cuts an electrical supply automatically when there is an overload, protecting against fire.

clue.text: Tax due she recklessly spent

indicators.note: recklessly suggests wild abandon, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman spent the money she owed in tax without care.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted means used up or worn out, just as spent does.

clue.text: It ensures one's words are discreet, so to speak

definitions.text: It ensures one's words are discreet, so to speak

parts.words: It ensures one's words are discreet, so to speak
parts.note: discreet said aloud is discrete, separate, and a keyboard key keeps typed words apart

explanation.surface: Something that keeps a person tactful in speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so to speak' warns that discreet stands for its sound-alike discrete, meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: This long key on a keyboard puts gaps between typed words.

clue.text: One achieves transfer of power by revolutionary means

definitions.text: One achieves transfer of power by revolutionary means

parts.words: One achieves transfer of power by revolutionary means
parts.note: not a political coup but a rotating rod carrying power from an engine

explanation.surface: A rebel who seizes power through revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer of power' and 'revolutionary' suggest a coup; the revolutions are turns of a rotating rod.
explanation.definitionFit: This rotating shaft transmits drive from a ship's engine to its screw.

clue.text: Casual cricket side needing help

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field
a hand is help, as in lend a hand

explanation.surface: A relaxed cricket team that could do with assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the off side is the half of the field facing the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand means casual or curt, done without much thought.

clue.text: Viability of attack on point of coast

indicators.note: on means the attack word sits above the coast word in this down clue

parts.note: a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Assessing whether an assault on a coastal headland can work.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitness means suitability or capability for a purpose.

clue.text: Little credit to academic stream in crucial period

parts.note: CR is the abbreviation of credit
the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford, the university city

explanation.surface: A little praise for a university stream at a decisive time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'academic stream' sounds like a school set; it is Oxford's river.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a turning point or time of acute danger.

clue.text: Restaurant Samuel Smiles would have recommended?

definitions.text: Restaurant Samuel Smiles would have recommended?

parts.words: Restaurant Samuel Smiles would have recommended?
parts.note: Samuel Smiles wrote the Victorian bestseller Self-Help, so he would favour a place where diners help themselves

explanation.surface: A Victorian moralist recommending somewhere to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Smiles was a Victorian author whose famous book was Self-Help.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service eating place, where customers collect their own food.

clue.text: Shot in the arm, given medical treatment

explanation.surface: An injection given as treatment by a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative medicine, and figuratively anything that gives a boost.

clue.text: Not qualified, so to speak

explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means complete or total; as a verb it means to say aloud.

clue.text: Jelly made from pork or beef

definitions.meaning: a cold meat set in jelly, made from a pig's head

explanation.surface: Choosing between pork and beef for a meat jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn is jellied pig's-head meat, and also muscular strength.

clue.text: In vain, having love?

definitions.meaning: in tennis a score of love means zero points

explanation.definitionFit: A pointless action is futile, and a love score literally has no points.

clue.text: Drink up, mate!

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the drinking word from bottom to top

parts.note: to lap is to drink with the tongue, like a cat

explanation.surface: A friendly toast: finish your glass, my friend!
explanation.definitionFit: Pal is informal for friend.

clue.text: Revolutionary principle that's fundamental

definitions.meaning: a root or basic element, from Latin radix, root

explanation.surface: A revolutionary idea that is at the root of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical means extreme in politics and also relating to the root of something.

clue.text: People from colonies one sees a lot of

definitions.text: People from colonies one sees a lot of

parts.words: People from colonies one sees a lot of
parts.note: not settlers from overseas colonies, but residents of naturist camps who wear no clothes

explanation.surface: Colonists one meets frequently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colonies' suggests the empire; 'sees a lot of' means sees much of their bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists live in so-called colonies and show a lot of bare skin.
